title: Third-Party Onboarding: Clauses Library + Risk QA Playbook (Draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a living playbook for legal + security + procurement to use when onboarding third-party vendors that will process Redwood Inference customer data or host model artifacts. Contains: 1) a short, modular clause library (DPA-adjacent snippets), 2) minimum security requirements and evidence checklist, and 3) an operator-friendly risk QA to run with vendors.

Scope and audience:
- Intended for use by Security & Compliance, Legal Business Partners, and Solutions/Procurement during commercial negotiations and onboarding gates.
- Focused on vendors who process customer data (PII, model inputs/outputs, embeddings, telemetry). Not exhaustive for regulated PHI/PCI (those require separate controls).

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Select the relevant clauses from the library. Prefer minimal edits; prefer adding an annex rather than changing core language.
2) Run the Risk QA with vendor engineering/security. Score responses per the scoring guide below.
3) Collect evidence artifacts (SOC2, architecture diagram, encryption config) and validate against the checklist.
4) If any red flags, escalate to Security & Compliance and Legal.

Clause Library (modular snippets - pick and paste into SOW/DPA annex):
A. Data Processing and Purpose Limitation
- "Vendor shall process Customer Data only for the purposes described in the Agreement and for no other purpose. Vendor will not access, use, or analyze Customer Data for its own product development, advertising, or model training unless expressly authorized in writing by Customer."

B. Subprocessors
- "Vendor may engage Subprocessors to perform processing activities on behalf of Customer. Vendor will provide a current list of Subprocessors upon request and will notify Customer at least thirty (30) days prior to the addition of any new Subprocessor performing data processing. Customer may object in writing within ten (10) days for legitimate security or regulatory reasons. If Customer objects, the Parties will cooperate in good faith to find an alternative solution (including termination of the relevant processing by Vendor)."

C. International Data Transfers
- "To the extent Customer Data is transferred outside the EEA/UK, Vendor will implement Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or equivalent lawful transfer mechanisms and will maintain documentation demonstrating compliance with applicable data transfer laws."

D. Encryption and Key Management
- "Vendor will encrypt Customer Data at rest and in transit using industry-accepted algorithms. Where Vendor manages encryption keys, Vendor will store keys in a hardware security module (HSM) or a customer-approved KMS. Any customer-managed key option must be documented and tested prior to production access."

E. Incident Notification and Forensics
- "Vendor will notify Customer of any confirmed security incident affecting Customer Data without undue delay and no later than 72 hours after Vendor becomes aware of the incident. Notification will include: (i) description of the incident and affected data classes, (ii) timeline, (iii) remediation actions taken, and (iv) proposed next steps. Vendor will provide reasonable cooperation to support Customer's regulatory obligations and will provide forensic reports on request under a mutually agreed SOW or NDA."

F. Data Retention, Deletion, and Return
- "Upon expiration or termination of the Agreement, Vendor will, at Customer's election, return or securely delete Customer Data within thirty (30) days and provide written certification of deletion. Backups containing Customer Data will be deleted or rendered inaccessible within ninety (90) days unless prohibited by applicable law."

G. Audit Rights and Evidence
- "Customer or an independent auditor (subject to reasonable confidentiality obligations) may audit Vendor's compliance with the Agreement once annually with reasonable notice. Vendor will provide relevant evidence including SOC reports, penetration test reports, change management logs, and network diagrams. Where an in-person audit is requested, Parties will coordinate scope and timing."

H. Liability and Insurance
- "Vendor will maintain commercial general liability insurance and cyber liability insurance with limits no less than $5,000,000 combined per occurrence annually. Vendor will notify Customer of any material changes to insurance coverage."

I. Model-Specific Handling (for vendors that host models or embeddings)
- "Vendor will not use customer-provided models or embeddings for training, benchmarking, or model improvement activities without explicit written consent. Any use of derived outputs for benchmarking must be aggregated and de-identified per the definitions in the Agreement."

Minimum Security Requirements (baseline for production vendors)
- Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256 or equivalent).
- Role-based access control (RBAC) + least privilege by default.
- MFA for all admin accounts.
- Logging and retention: security logs retained for at least 90 days, with ability to export on request.
- Vulnerability management: monthly vulnerability scans, triage SLA for critical findings (7 days).
- Penetration testing: annual third-party pentest with executive summary and remediation plan.
- Proven secure SDLC practices (code review, SCA for dependencies).
- Backup and restore testing cadence and recovery point objectives (RPO) / recovery time objectives (RTO) declared.

Evidence artifacts we ask for during onboarding (samples):
- SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate (if available).
- Network architecture diagram showing segmentation and data flows.
- List of current subprocessors and their country of operations.
- Encryption configuration: algorithms, key custodian, KMS/HSM proof.
- Recent pen test summary and remediation plan.
- Sample incident report (redacted).
- Data retention policy and deletion proof flowchart.
- Cyber insurance declaration page.

Onboarding Gate Checklist (suggested flow - gate by gate):
1) Procurement gate: commercial terms, initial questionnaires completed, business justification.
2) Security gate: vendor answers QA + evidence upload, scoring done. If score >= threshold, proceed.
3) Legal gate: DPA/clauses inserted and approved.
4) Production gate: final network/ops onboarding, secrets/keys exchange (if applicable), internal rollout plan.

Vendor Risk QA (operator-friendly - run with vendor security engineer; score each answer 0/1/2):
- Scoring guide: 0 = unacceptable/major gap, 1 = partial/conditional, 2 = meets expectation. Total normalized to 100. Recommended thresholds: >=85 pass, 70-85 conditional with compensating controls, <70 require remediation or alternate vendor.

Questions (short form for initial technical call):
1) Do you encrypt customer data at rest? If yes, which algorithm and who controls keys?
2) Do you offer customer-managed keys (CMK)? If not, describe key separation controls.
3) Are there any subprocessors that will access live customer data? Provide names and locations.
4) Do you maintain SOC2 Type II or ISO27001? If yes, provide most recent report or certificate.
5) Describe your incident detection and response timeline and tooling (SIEM, EDR).
6) How do you segregate customer data in multi-tenant environments?
7) Is there any routine human review of model outputs that contain customer data?
8) Do you use customer data to train or fine-tune models? If yes, explain consent and opt-out model.
9) How are backups protected and how long are they retained?
10) Do you support data deletion APIs for automated purge? If so, explain retention guarantees.
11) Provide your vulnerability management cadence and SLA for critical vulnerability remediation.
12) Provide details on your pentest provider and date of last test.
13) Describe admin access controls and privileged access monitoring.
14) What logging/telemetry do you collect from customer workloads? Who can access logs?
15) Describe your business continuity and disaster recovery plans (RPO/RTO).
16) Do you maintain cyber insurance? Provide limits and insurer name.
17) Describe any third-country transfers and mechanisms used (SCCs, adequacy, etc.).
18) Are there any encryption backdoors, law enforcement access, or other exceptional access mechanisms?
19) What is your data minimization policy for telemetry and logs?
20) Provide sample redacted incident report or incident timeline example.

Scoring notes / red flags:
- Vendor refuses any annual audit or refuses to provide SOC2/ISO evidence -> automatic red flag (score 0).
- No encryption at rest or weak algorithms -> critical.
- Vendor-managed keys without HSM or strong key separation -> conditional (accept only if compensating controls like dedicated tenancy are in place).
- New subprocessors in high-risk countries without SCCs -> escalate.

Negotiation tips for Legal and Security partners:
- Try to move vendor to accept Vendor-managed DPA annex instead of editing Redwood's master DPA heavily. Faster, preserves controls.
- Insist on 30-day subprocessor notice with opt-out for high-risk vendors.
- Use customer-managed keys or VPC/private deployment as leverage when data sensitivity is high.
- If vendor pushes to use data for product improvement, require opt-in and explicit limits (no training on customer inputs without a separate agreement).

Open questions / items to standardize (todo):
- Standard preferred cyber insurance limit for high-impact systems (raise to $10M?)
- Template for a short-form attestation when SOC2 is not available (what evidence acceptable?).
- Clarify timeline for deletion of backups where backups cross jurisdictions (90-day default currently).

Appendix: Sample DPA Annex (compact - to be used when fast onboarding is required)
- Include shortened clauses A-I above with placeholders: [Customer], [Vendor], [Subprocessor List URL], [SCCs attached if applicable].

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: we prefer clear gates and objective evidence over open-ended contractual language that vendors push back on.
- Share feedback in the linked CONFLUENCE-3921 page and tag Security & Legal channel in Slack for urgent escalations.

Quick reference links (internal):
- Confluence: Employee onboarding flow for vendors: CONFLUENCE-3921
- Procurement playbook: CONFLUENCE-0501
- Incident classification matrix: CONFLUENCE-3310

(End of draft — do not finalize without Legal sign-off)
